channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Uganda plans new railway line to Tanzania, opening up new export route
item.description: Uganda is considering linking a new railway line it is developing to a separate line under construction in neighbouring Tanzania.

item.title: US expands its tent in Africa with new energy and minerals financing
item.description: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation has approved a fresh round of strategic investments across Africa, sharpening Washington’s economic focus on critical minerals, energy security, and regional stability.

item.title: Somaliland offers U.S. exclusive mineral access, military bases in exchange for statehood recognition
item.description: Somaliland has offered the United States exclusive access to key mineral deposits and the possibility of hosting American military facilities, as the self-declared republic intensifies efforts to secure international recognition amid a shifting geopolitical landscape in the Horn of Africa.

item.title: Africa’s largest aviation hub closes doors to foreign rivals, equips local airlines to compete internationally
item.description: Ethiopia has ruled out an immediate full opening of its aviation market to foreign private airlines, signalling a strategic push to strengthen domestic operators before exposing them to global competition.

item.title: US visa clampdown on Africa spares Nigerian students as full details emerge
item.description: Nigerian students and exchange visitors currently holding valid F-1 and J-1 visas will not be affected by the United States’ partial visa suspension, according to the United States Mission Nigeria.

item.title: South African immigration officials accepted bribes for visas for 20 years, new government report reveals
item.description: A new government probe has uncovered organised corruption within South Africa’s immigration department, revealing that officials took payments for visa approvals between 2004 and 2024.

item.title: Billionaire to president? South Africa’s richest black man is said to be stepping into politics
item.description: Despite the fact that South Africa’s wealthiest black billionaire, Patrice Motsepe, has consistently dismissed rumors of any political aspirations, recent speculation has surfaced suggesting he intends to contest for the presidency of one of the country's most prominent political parties.

item.title: From cannabis possession to attempted murder, another Mugabe finds himself in legal trouble
item.description: Last year in October, Robert Mugabe Jr, 33, the son of Zimbabwe’s ex-president, Robert Mugabe, was arrested in Harare after police said they found cannabis in his bag during a traffic stop. Very recently, his brother, Bellarmine Mugabe, 28, was arrested in connection with a murder.

item.title: Two Nigerian industrialists handily outperform other top-level African billionaires
item.description: According to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, two Nigerian industrialists, Aliko Dangote and Abdulsamad Rabiu, have emerged as Africa's best-performing billionaires in the first two months of the year.

item.title: Elumelu-backed Seplat deal fuels $1.25bn value surge, signals fresh energy momentum
item.description: Shares of Seplat Energy Plc have surged sharply after Heirs Energies Limited struck a landmark acquisition backed by billionaire investor Tony Elumelu, adding roughly $1.25 billion to the company's market value and energising sentiment on the Nigerian bourse.
